_about: ONE machine-readable source for harness capabilities in MC. Edit this file, then run: python3 tools/render-harness-matrix.py. Guards: backend/tests/test_harness_matrix.py (columns vs. code, doc drift, evidence) and backend/tests/test_harness_dev_ring.py (ring section).
intro: What every harness can do in Mission Control, and how mature it is — one place, so nobody has to dig the facts together again.

- **Source:** [`docs/harness-matrix.json`](harness-matrix.json) — the per-harness matrix below **and** the dev-ring declarations of [harness-dev-ring.md](harness-dev-ring.md) (24 task capabilities per harness × place).

- **Guard:** `backend/tests/test_harness_matrix.py` turns red when a harness known in code has no column, when this file drifts from the source, or when cited evidence no longer exists. `backend/tests/test_harness_dev_ring.py` guards the ring section.
- Columns are the harnesses MC knows in code (`harness_compat`, `host_harness_adapter`, `compose_renderer`) plus the terminal session of ADR-100 stage 2c.

maturity_levels.stable: in daily use and covered by tests; changes need the normal gates
maturity_levels.beta: shipped and working, not yet proven in daily use
maturity_levels.experimental: wired in code, never proven end to end
maturity_levels.frozen: kept and guarded, no new features (quiet mode, ADR-085) — or on its way out

how_to_change: 1. Edit `docs/harness-matrix.json` (a new harness: add a column, a cell in every row, and — for an agent harness — its dev-ring rows).
2. Every `yes` / `partial` cell cites `path:line` or `live:YYYY-MM-DD <what was measured>`; every `no` carries `since` + `recheck`; unknown is `open`, never a guess.
3. Run `python3 tools/render-harness-matrix.py` and commit both files. `backend/tests/test_harness_matrix.py` fails until you do.
